data_center.body: Available records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the 3,068 operating sites; 894 sites are in the tracked active pipeline. Recent reports show individual large projects moving forward: Fluidstack began construction on a 99-acre campus in Virginia, and Fluor won the engineering, procurement and construction contract for a $4 billion Kentucky campus. These projects show activity reaching the construction and contracting stages, but they do not measure the conversion rate of the national pipeline.
data_center.headline: Campus projects move into contracting and construction while 1,556 sites remain in development

finance.body: Operating cash flow is 1.23 times current CapEx, while cash reserves equal 0.85 years of spending at the current pace. Borrower strain, at 25.8, is above lender strain at 21.0. Bloomberg reported that BBVA is considering a risk-transfer transaction to hedge about $500 million of data-center loans. The report concerns one lender and does not establish system-wide credit stress, but it shows explicit risk management around data-center exposure.
finance.headline: Current cash flow covers capital spending, but reserves provide less than a year of coverage

macro.body: Capital formation is running alongside a large physical development pipeline. Information-processing investment growth rose materially to 22.7%, almost matching 22.9% growth in computer and peripheral-equipment output. Available records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the 3,068 sites already operating. The expansion is visible in measured investment, equipment output and site-development records. Internal cash generation supports the current spending rate, but the reserve margin is limited. Operating cash flow is 1.23 times current CapEx, while cash reserves equal 0.85 years of CapEx at the current pace. Bloomberg reported that BBVA is weighing a risk-transfer transaction for about $500 million of data-center loans. That is not evidence of broad credit deterioration, but it shows how at least one lender is considering explicit protection against data-center exposure. Grid delivery remains the harder part of execution. The active interconnection queue totals 2,061 GW, but only 24.2% has reached executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Data Center Dynamics reported that Cheyenne Light applied to build transmission infrastructure for three Microsoft data centers in Wyoming. The filing illustrates project-specific planning around large loads, but an application remains short of a working grid connection. The scale of investment is clearer than the timing of usable capacity.
macro.headline: Investment momentum is strong, while funding depth and grid delivery remain the execution tests

market.body: The AI Equity Index slipped to 33.4, while average sector trading pressure rose slightly to 40.0. Median and equal-weight one-year returns also edged down, to 7.3% and 8.1%. CNBC reported that Palo Alto Networks shares surged after an earnings beat, higher guidance and a $4.5 billion AI deal. That response shows that concrete company news can still produce sharp gains even as broader measures soften.
market.headline: Broad AI equity measures soften despite a sharp company-specific gain

power.body: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, nearly twice the 1.8% increase in total retail demand, while retail electricity prices are up 5.1%. Net planned generation additions total 227.1 GW through the pipeline horizon, but planned supply is not delivered capacity. Utility Dive reported that TVA touted a $1.7 billion data-center deal under a new large-load tariff. The agreement is a concrete sign of utility contracting for a major load, but one deal does not resolve the timing of the broader generation pipeline.
power.headline: Commercial power demand outpaces the total as TVA reports a tariff-backed data-center deal

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The AI Equity Index increased materially to 35.4. The median one-year return rose to 8.8%, and 61.8% of covered companies now show positive one-year returns. Because both the median and the positive-return share improved materially, the advance is broader than an index gain alone. Average sector trading pressure still edged up to 41.8, so the stronger return profile did not coincide with lower trading pressure.

headline.text: AI equity gains broaden as the median return and positive breadth rise

body.text: Lender strain decreased materially to 16.4, leaving it well below borrower strain at 25.8. Operating cash flow covers current CapEx 1.23 times, while cash reserves equal 0.85 years of spending at the current pace. The latest reading combines lower pressure on lenders with enough internal cash generation to cover current investment, but borrowers remain more strained and the reserve buffer is limited.

headline.text: Lender strain falls, but cash reserves still cover less than a year of CapEx

body.text: Available records list 1,556 sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the 3,068 operating sites. Investor's Business Daily reported that SpaceX won a permit for a $24 billion Texas data-center project, while Data Center Dynamics reported that Galaxy Digital filed for the next development phase at its Helios campus in Texas. These are concrete steps for two projects, but a permit and a phase filing remain short of operating capacity.

headline.text: Texas data-center projects move through permitting and phased development

body.text: Total retail electricity demand growth increased materially to 2.5%, while commercial demand growth reached 4.1%. Retail price growth slowed materially to 3.5%. Net planned generation additions total 227.1 GW through the pipeline horizon, but planned supply remains distinct from delivered capacity. The latest balance is stronger demand with slower price growth, while the timing of new generation remains an execution issue.

headline.text: Electricity demand accelerates while retail price growth slows
The development pipeline remains large as power demand accelerates and delivery stays uncertain

paragraphs.text: Physical development remains extensive. Available records list 1,556 data-center sites in development, equal to 0.51 times the 3,068-site operating base. Investor's Business Daily reported that SpaceX won a permit for a $24 billion Texas project, and Data Center Dynamics reported that Galaxy Digital filed for the next phase of its Helios campus. The reports show individual projects progressing through permitting and phased development, not that the full pipeline has converted into operating capacity.

Current finance and market measures are firmer, though the funding buffer is not deep. Operating cash flow covers current CapEx 1.23 times, and lender strain fell materially to 16.4, below borrower strain of 25.8. Cash reserves equal 0.85 years of current CapEx. In equities, 61.8% of covered companies have positive one-year returns, and the median return rose materially to 8.8%. The readings show broader equity performance and current internal funding coverage, not a large reserve cushion.

Electricity demand is strengthening alongside the development pipeline: total retail demand growth accelerated to 2.5%, and commercial demand growth reached 4.1%, while retail price growth slowed to 3.5%. Net planned generation additions total 227.1 GW, but the interconnection record argues against treating pipeline capacity as delivered supply. Only 24.2% of the 2,061 GW active queue is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. The scale of planned supply is clear; the timing of usable capacity remains uncertain.

You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.
